neighbours.label: The link that explains how something is known or done in expository science writing (because we observe, is done by, we use it to make), vs science sentences that state facts without a cause or means link
fire: Geologists know the continents have moved because they find matching fossils on distant coasts.
Copper conducts electricity well, which is why engineers use it to make household wiring.
These days the mapping of ocean depths is mostly done by sonar mounted on ships.
Chemists can identify the gas because they measure the colors of light it absorbs.
Silica melts at high heat, so manufacturers use it to make glass for windows.
In modern labs the counting of cells is largely done by automated machines.
Biologists conclude the birds migrate at night because they detect them on weather radar.
Rubber stretches without breaking, which is why factories use it to make tires.
quiet: Geologists study the continents and the fossils found on distant coasts.
Copper is a reddish metal found in many old coins and household pipes.
The oceans are very deep in some places and shallow in others.
Chemists in the lab wore goggles while working with the gas.
Silica is a common mineral found in sand on many beaches.
The modern lab has bright lights and several large freezers for cells.
Biologists watched the birds gather in the trees near the lake at dusk.
Rubber trees grow in warm climates with plenty of rain.

predictions: Fire 0.3-0.7 on because/by/to make in explanatory science prose; near misses in the same topics without the explanatory link under 0.15.
notes: Card: because, by, made, of, from, evident, observation, studying. Probe: 'because they observe stars orbiting nothing visible' 0.670, 'which is why we use it to make pencils' 0.572, 'mostly done by satellites' 0.453, 'consequence of this observation' 0.238; 'became evident that the engine' 0.085, everyday sentences 0.02-0.03.
